title: Reserve Beacon: Predictive Burst Planner & Health Roster
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design ticket for a compact, operator-focused dashboard panel (Reserve Beacon) that combines predictive burst planning, live GPU pool health roster, and lightweight autoscale controls for Dedicated capacity customers. Goal: give SREs and platform operators a single surface to preview upcoming burst windows, simulate cost/latency impact, and perform quick emergency overrides without leaving the Console. Scope includes layout exploration, state transitions, micro-interactions, accessibility pass, and a high-fidelity Figma prototype for handoff. Success metrics: reduce mean time to resolution (MTTR) for capacity incidents by 25% in pilot customers; shorten common burst configuration tasks to under 90 seconds in usability tests.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Figma prototype linked and annotated for all states (idle, planning, active burst, degraded). 2) Accessible keyboard flows and aria attributes documented. 3) Usability test with 6 operators shows median completion under 90s for 'schedule a burst' and 'apply emergency throttle'. 4) Hand-off ticket with annotated tokens and spacing delivered to ENG and a PR created referencing this design. 5) PM sign-off on cost simulation accuracy model and fallback UX.
design_notes: Key design decisions and trade-offs: (a) Combined timeline+roster instead of separate views to minimize context switches; trade-off: denser visual layout requiring condensed state labels. (b) Inline cost estimator uses simplified unit rates; detailed billing links out to Cost Explorer to avoid duplicating billing logic. (c) Emergency override flows are intentionally modal-first with clear countdowns rather than inline toggles to prevent accidental activation. (d) Prototype uses 'soft' confirmations for canary bursts and a required two-step for cluster-wide reservations. Consideration for low-bandwidth regions: UI falls back to text-only roster with stream updates throttled.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Kickoff: Align with PM (Lena Park) and ENG infra lead (Diego Martinez) on scope. Agreed to prioritize predictive burst planner over historical analytics for MVP.

2026-02-20 - Explorations complete: 3 layout variants (stacked timeline, split-pane roster, compact ribbon). Team favored split-pane roster for scanability. Recorded decision in Confluence (see attachments).

2026-02-26 - Mid-fi review: Design critique with Platform Eng. Feedback: expose current autoscale policy name and link to policy editor; add explicit 'compatibility check' when scheduling bursts across heterogeneous GPU types. Action: add compatibility badge and API contract note for ENG.

2026-03-03 - UX Research: Moderated usability sessions (n=6 operators). Findings: users appreciated quick cost preview but requested clearer signal for 'estimated queue time' under heavy load. Added a latency forecast strip and tooltip explaining confidence intervals.
2026-03-07 - Security & compliance sync: Confirmed no extra data residency needs; audit log entries required for every manual override. Added audit hook spec to handoff notes.

2026-03-10 - Engineering handoff pre-PR: Created implementation checklist and proposed API shape for burst scheduling (ENG owners: Diego Martinez, Priya Nair). Link to GH PR in attachments. ENG requested smaller CSS footprint for Console; noted for dev handoff.
2026-03-12 - Design review: PM approved visual language; requested one additional microcopy pass for error states. Updated prototype and re-uploaded.
2026-03-12 - Next: Prepare final handoff package and open implementation tickets for split-pane roster, timeline simulator, cost estimator, autoscale control microflows.
